title: He Left India at 23 to Study Computer Science. Now an Oscar-Winning Producer Has Made a Film About His Cricket.
excerpt: Saurabh Netravalkar's journey from Mumbai's maidans to Silicon Valley to the T20 World Cup is the subject of 'The Long Game,' premiering June 17 on Willow TV and Amazon Prime Video.
body:
In the summer of 2024, Saurabh Netravalkar bowled the Super Over that changed American cricket forever. The United States had just tied with Pakistan in the group stage of the T20 World Cup in Dallas, and the left-arm seamer from Mumbai was handed the ball for the tiebreaker. He conceded just 13 runs. The USA won, Pakistan were stunned, and Netravalkar — a 32-year-old software engineer at Oracle — became an overnight sensation across two continents.

Two years later, his story is getting the feature-length treatment. *The Long Game: Saurabh Netravalkar, Between Two Worlds* premieres on June 17 on Willow TV and debuts on Amazon Prime Video the following day, timed to the opening of the 2026 Major League Cricket season.

## From Mumbai Maidans to Cornell

The documentary, directed by Pierre Friquet, traces Netravalkar's arc from the dusty grounds of Mumbai, where he played alongside future Indian internationals, to the manicured lawns of American club cricket. He represented India at the Under-19 World Cup in 2010 but never broke into the senior team. By 2015, he had moved to the United States to pursue a master's degree at Cornell University.

For years, cricket was something he did on weekends, quietly, while building a career in tech. His colleagues at Oracle had no idea their coworker was flying across the country to play in tournaments. He debuted for the USA in 2019, and his dual existence — code by day, cricket by evening — became the central tension of his life.

"I actually had tears in my eyes when I watched it," Netravalkar told Reuters about seeing the completed documentary. "I'm very comfortable being a raw version of myself and just put it out there."

## An Oscar Winner Behind the Camera

The film is produced by Adam Leipzig, the Academy Award-winning producer whose 2006 documentary *March of the Penguins* won the Oscar for Best Documentary Feature. *The Long Game* marks Leipzig's 40th feature film and represents Willow TV's first foray into premium original storytelling beyond live sports broadcasting.

"Saurabh represents a kind of determination and clarity that reaches far beyond cricket," Leipzig said in a press release. "Whether you know the sport or not, this is a story about persistence, identity and achieving something that once felt impossible."

Friquet's direction weaves the climactic Super Over against Pakistan with pivotal moments from Netravalkar's personal history. The film uses animation to recreate what it calls "nightmare sequences" — the internal voices that told him he would never make it as a cricketer, never follow his passion.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRIs in the United States and Canada, Netravalkar's story resonates on multiple frequencies. He is the immigrant who kept a childhood dream alive while navigating the H-1B visa system, building a career in Big Tech, and integrating into a country where cricket is still a fringe pursuit. His journey from India's U-19 setup to America's senior team mirrors a path many in the diaspora understand: the reinvention, the quiet persistence, the eventual recognition.

Willow TV's short documentary *American Cricket*, which served as a precursor to *The Long Game*, recently earned three Telly Awards, including Silver wins in the General-Sports and General-Unscripted categories.

## Eyes on LA 2028

At 34, Netravalkar is not slowing down. His next ambition is the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, where cricket will return to the Games for the first time since 1900. As the host nation, the USA are expected to receive an automatic berth.

"Whether we qualify as hosts or through the qualification pathway, the goal is to be there," Netravalkar has said. He credits his analytical training in tech — pattern recognition, disciplined problem-solving — as a quiet advantage on the cricket field.

The 2026 MLC season, which begins the day after the documentary debuts on Amazon Prime Video, will be his most high-profile domestic campaign yet. For the Indian-American community, *The Long Game* is a rare thing: a feature-length film that understands both halves of the hyphen.

*The Long Game: Saurabh Netravalkar, Between Two Worlds premieres June 17 on Willow TV and June 18 on Amazon Prime Video.*
